title: Foundations: Rocksteady - The Complete Guide
summary: What Rocksteady is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Rocksteady songs: Reggae is Jamaica's gift to the world: the skank guitar chopping on the offbeat, deep one-drop drums, bass as melody, and lyrics of faith, struggle, and unity. Bob Marley made it a global language.

History: From ska (early 1960s) through rocksteady (1966–68) to reggae (1968+): Toots, the Wailers, and producers like Lee 'Scratch' Perry built it. Marley's 1970s Island albums took it worldwide; dub invented the remix.

How the songs work: Rocksteady favors the keys of G, C, D, A, Em. Common forms include Verse-chorus with dub-wise breakdowns; Toasting: DJ talking over the rhythm. Players should master the skank: muted guitar chops on beats 2 and 4 first, then one-drop drums: kick and snare together on beat 3. Guitar chops in open positions.

title: Rocksteady Etude No. 1: Roots i–VII–VI–VII
summary: An original Rocksteady study in C drilling one-drop drums: kick and snare together on beat 3.
body:
This original etude isolates the 'Roots i–VII–VI–VII' progression in the key of C — the changes Rocksteady players must know cold.

CHART:
Cm | A# | G# | A#

FORM: toasting: dj talking over the rhythm.

PRACTICE: loop the chart slowly, adding one-drop drums: kick and snare together on beat 3 once the changes are clean. Then transpose with the included program and drill it in all twelve keys — the Rocksteady player's rite of passage.

title: No Woman, No Cry - Rocksteady Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for No Woman, No Cry by Bob Marley (1974).
body:
No Woman, No Cry — Bob Marley, 1974. Live at the Lyceum; the world sings along.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of D):
D | Bm | Em | A7

This study chart uses the 'Rocksteady I–vi–ii–V' progression, the Rocksteady workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus with dub-wise breakdowns. Listen for bass playing the melody — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Rocksteady pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let bass playing the melody. Guitar chops in open positions. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
